reason: Checked and confirmed at 04:25Z. Win32_Process shows PID 16292 (parent 13516, created 00:47Z). Its loop is `until last | grep -qE "^(56656147|56656157|56657612),.*(COMPLETE|ERROR)"`, so it is one-shot on ANY of the three refs, and no other process watches them. The poll header at 04:24:30Z shows all three PENDING. exp89p reads first (07:38-08:35Z), so 16292 will fire on exp89p. The live timer.sh jobs are due at 07:13/07:23/08:13/08:30/09:13/10:13/11:10Z, with nothing between 09:13 and 10:13Z. exp89r (~09:25-09:35Z) and exp75 (09:05-10:05Z) complete inside that gap. The 02:53Z (1) A-M2 function and freeze (6) put the decision and submit at exp89r's first terminal header. No logged step re-arms a night-ref watcher: R30-A2 covers only the morning submits, and the 02:53Z (5) re-arm is for the watchdog. So unless the session re-arms by habit, A-M2 falls to the 10:13Z round or the 11:10Z backstop. For a non-CI file with L 7.0-7.8 h, that moves the read from ~16:40-17:30Z to as late as ~18:15-19:05Z, past the 18:37Z FINAL proposal. The arithmetic holds. The value is procedural but real: A-M2 can produce a new V_pub, and the timing risk sits right on the finals. The fix is local-only: 0 Kaggle calls, a grep every 120 s, no rule change, no R1-R10 conflict, and duplicate firing is harmless. One defect in the proposed command: `cut -c1-220` truncates the exp89r row, which is 266 chars. The cut drops 'SubmissionStatus.COMPLETE,<score>', so the wake message would not show the display the A-M2 function needs.
fix:
Arm the two run_in_background watchers now, but reuse 16292's formatter instead of cut. For exp89r: cd "/c/Users/vital/Documents/kAGGLE/Biohub - Cell Tracking During Development" && last(){ awk '/^=== /{blk=""} {blk=blk"
"$0} END{print blk}' experiments/lb_poll/poll.log; }; until last | grep -qE "^56656147,.*(COMPLETE|ERROR)"; do sleep 120; done; date -u +%H:%M:%S; last | grep -E "^===|^(56656147|56656157|56657612)," | awk -F'SubmissionStatus.' '{print substr($1,1,50), $2}'. Arm the same with 56656157 for exp75. When the exp89r watcher fires, first re-read that header in full from poll.log (d_R, d_P, failed-attempt count for L_hi). Then apply 02:53Z (1) and nb_try at once. Log one line in CONTEXT stating that night-ref watchers are re-armed per ref, as ops only with no rule change.
realistic_gain: No score change. The gain is that A-M2 is decided at exp89r's first terminal header (~09:25-09:45Z) and not at 10:13Z or 11:10Z. That gives the M2 file's read ~40-100 min earlier (~16:40-17:30Z, not up to ~19:05Z), before the 18:37Z FINAL proposal. It only matters in the minority of branches where A-M2 is not UNUSED (DIS '+', or Rr '+' with DIS '?' and P '+'/'?'). It also brings the exp75 partner-rule read forward for the 12:03Z card.
